references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 1.7–1.12, 1.14–1.15

sections.heading: Formation and identifying the enterprise
sections.body: A general partnership is identified by a co-owned business for profit, not merely by the label on a document. An express agreement helps establish the relationship, but conduct may show an implied arrangement. Separate the evidence of profit participation from the ability to participate in important management decisions. An agreement that profit shares compensate a loan or services can have a different legal effect from an ownership arrangement. A joint venture generally concerns a narrower project or shorter duration, but its essential co-ownership and control questions resemble partnership questions.

sections.heading: Liability and organization are separate inquiries
sections.body: A limited partnership uses a statutory formation process and separates general-partner and limited-partner positions. Identify the governing statute before applying the fifth edition’s historical discussion of limited-partner participation in management. An LLC combines an entity liability shield with an operating agreement and statutory defaults. Determine whether members manage directly or have appointed managers; the word member alone does not establish authority to transact. An entity shield does not answer whether a person is liable for that person’s own conduct or separate contractual undertaking.

sections.heading: Contract, tax, and less familiar forms
sections.body: The LLC operating agreement supplies negotiated rules on governance, transfers, duration, and exits, subject to nonwaivable statutory limits. Read the statute and agreement together rather than assuming corporate defaults apply. The book contrasts pass-through treatment with entity-level taxation and possible owner-level tax on distributions; its historical tax eligibility numbers should not be reused as current advice. Joint stock companies can offer centralized management and transferable interests without the corporate liability shield. In a business trust, trustees hold legal title and manage assets for beneficial owners under the declaration of trust.

sections.heading: Exam method and comparison
sections.body: Build a separate row for formation, management, owner exposure, transferability, duration, and tax treatment for each candidate form. On a lender-control problem, identify which provisions merely protect repayment and which give the lender meaningful participation as an owner. Do not equate economic dependence, a profit-based return, or a veto by itself with partnership. In an LLC problem, quote the operating-agreement term that displaces a default and identify any mandatory rule preventing displacement. The point is to explain the legal consequences of the facts, not select a label based only on the parties’ preferred terminology.

examQuestions.question: Hypothetical: A lender receives a profit-based return and a veto over unusually risky borrowing. Does that alone establish a partnership?
examQuestions.answer: No. Evaluate the whole arrangement for co-ownership and meaningful management participation. Profit-based loan compensation and protective restrictions are evidence to evaluate, not automatic ownership.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Non-Traditional Corporations
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 1.16–1.18, 1.20–1.21, 1.23

sections.heading: Different classification questions
sections.body: Governmental or municipal corporations must be distinguished from private business corporations. A publicly held company is not necessarily a public governmental body: publicly held ordinarily concerns dispersed ownership and market trading of shares. Closely held describes ownership and the absence of a ready public market, not simply a business’s small size. A substantial enterprise can remain closely held. These classifications answer different questions and should not be treated as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Nonprofit organization and economic activity
sections.body: Nonprofit corporate status concerns the organization’s purposes and restrictions on distributing benefits; it does not establish that the entity never receives revenue, owns valuable property, or pays employees. Identify the statutory category and permitted beneficiaries. Keep incorporation under nonprofit law separate from tax exemption. A conclusion about one does not automatically establish the other. Start with the actual organizational statute and governing documents rather than the everyday meaning of charity.

sections.heading: Concentrated control and professional entities
sections.body: A corporation may have one shareholder, be family controlled, or be owned wholly or partly by a parent company. Sole ownership does not automatically erase the entity. Minority-investor risks arise where a controller can shape compensation, distributions, and exit opportunities. Professional corporations and professional LLCs add licensing constraints: the organizational form cannot authorize unlicensed practice. Distinguish a professional’s own service-related responsibility from exposure based solely on being an investor in the firm.

sections.heading: Analysis checklist
sections.body: Ask who created the entity, what statutory purpose it serves, who holds ownership rights, whether a trading market exists, and whether occupational licensing limits ownership or management. For a parent-subsidiary problem, preserve the distinction between ownership control and the additional facts needed to disregard separate entities. For a nonprofit, do not infer tax exemption from the charter label. Use the classification to identify the applicable legal rules rather than treating classification itself as the answer to every liability question.

examQuestions.question: A company has thousands of shareholders and publicly traded shares. Is it therefore a governmental corporation?
examQuestions.answer: No. Public trading describes ownership and market characteristics; governmental status concerns its creation, purpose, and governing public law. Analyze the classifications separately.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Agency
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 1.24, 8.1, 8.5, 8.10, 8.12
guides.scope: The supplied fifth edition matches the outline. These notes cover the identified topics, not every proposition in every assigned section. Historical statutory and tax discussions are not a statement of current law.

sections.heading: Actual authority
sections.body: A corporation can act only through human agents. Actual authority concerns the principal’s communications to the agent and the powers reasonably included in the assignment. Read the charter, bylaws, board resolutions, delegated responsibilities, and established course of dealing. Express authorization for a task can include incidental acts needed to accomplish it. Distinguish the existence of authority from whether the agent complied with internal instructions; a departure can matter differently to the agent and the third party.

sections.heading: Apparent authority and transaction type
sections.body: Apparent authority concerns the principal’s manifestations to a third party and the resulting reasonable understanding of the agent’s authority. An agent cannot establish it merely by asserting that authority exists. A president or CEO may have authority to carry out ordinary business through express delegation, implied responsibilities, or the corporation’s acquiescence. The title does not automatically authorize extraordinary transactions. Explain why the transaction is ordinary or exceptional in the business’s context.

sections.heading: Ratification and evidence
sections.body: Ratification addresses an originally unauthorized act that the principal later adopts with the legally required knowledge and intent. It is an alternative to proving authority existed at the time of contracting. Acceptance of benefits may matter, but identify what the corporation knew and what conduct communicated adoption. For a major conveyance, mortgage, or long-term commitment, the book recommends obtaining formal evidence such as a certified board resolution rather than relying only on an officer’s assurance.

sections.heading: Exam structure
sections.body: Identify the alleged principal, agent, third party, transaction, and relevant time. Analyze actual authority first, apparent authority separately, then ratification or estoppel if supported. For apparent authority, identify the principal’s particular manifestation and why reliance on it was reasonable. An internal restriction unknown to the third party is not necessarily dispositive. Conclude separately about the corporation’s obligation and any claim concerning the agent’s unauthorized conduct.

examQuestions.question: A CEO signs an extraordinary asset transaction after merely telling the buyer that the board authorized it. Is apparent authority established?
examQuestions.answer: Not by the agent’s assertion alone. Identify a manifestation by the corporation and reasonable third-party reliance, examine actual delegation, and distinguish ordinary operations from an extraordinary transaction.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Introduction to Corporations
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 1.10, 2.1–2.9, 7.1–7.2, 9.1
guides.scope: The supplied fifth edition matches the outline. These notes cover the identified topics, not every proposition in every assigned section. Historical statutory and tax discussions are not a statement of current law.

sections.heading: Entity and investors
sections.body: Corporate personality means that the corporation holds its own assets and contractual rights and bears its own obligations. A shareholder owns an equity interest rather than a fraction of each corporate asset. Keep limited liability analytically separate from that entity status: the corporation can owe a debt without its shareholders automatically owing the debt. Ownership changes ordinarily do not require the corporation to transfer every asset or renegotiate every obligation.

sections.heading: Governance structure
sections.body: The conventional arrangement gives shareholders the power to elect directors and vote on specified fundamental matters; the board directs or oversees corporate affairs; officers conduct delegated operations. A shareholder majority is not automatically authorized to make every management decision directly. Conversely, the board’s broad management role is not a license to ignore shareholder votes required by statute or governing documents. State which institution has initial authority and what approvals the specific transaction requires.

sections.heading: Historical development and enabling law
sections.body: The assigned history explains the transition from special governmental grants toward general incorporation statutes and greater organizational flexibility. The practical drafting consequence is to distinguish mandatory rules from defaults that may be changed in the charter or bylaws. Do not use the history to assume that every present statute is identical. The entity’s state of incorporation supplies the starting framework for its internal governance.

sections.heading: Worked analysis method
sections.body: When an owner orders an officer to sign an agreement, identify whether the owner is acting as shareholder, director, officer, or a specially authorized agent. Then determine whether that capacity supplies the power asserted. A person may occupy several roles, but the legal consequences of each role differ. For a tax question, distinguish the entity’s state-law form from its tax classification and flag the historical scope of the assigned edition.

examQuestions.question: A shareholder owns every share and claims personal ownership of each corporate asset. What distinction is missing?
examQuestions.answer: The corporation owns its assets; the shareholder owns an equity interest. Sole ownership does not automatically erase entity separateness or determine liability for corporate obligations.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Selection of Corporate Form
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 1.5–1.6, 3.1–3.2
guides.scope: The supplied fifth edition matches the outline. These notes cover the identified topics, not every proposition in every assigned section. Historical statutory and tax discussions are not a statement of current law.

sections.heading: Choosing a legal form
sections.body: Selection is a comparison of legal and practical consequences, not a universal preference for incorporation. Identify who will invest, who will manage, how much personal exposure participants accept, the expected duration of the venture, and how an owner can leave. Financing and transfer needs may favor an entity with stable centralized governance. Tax treatment, administrative expense, and the parties’ appetite for negotiated arrangements also matter. A form suitable at inception may require later conversion as the business changes.

sections.heading: Choosing the organizing state
sections.body: The incorporating jurisdiction supplies not just statutory provisions but the case law on directors’ duties and investor rights. A local business may incur unnecessary costs by incorporating elsewhere: foreign qualification, recurring filings, fees, taxes, and counsel’s need to use unfamiliar law. A larger interstate enterprise may have stronger reasons to select another jurisdiction. Explain the actual tradeoff rather than asserting that a familiar corporate domicile is always best.

sections.heading: Documents and operation
sections.body: Distinguish the place of formation from the places where the business conducts activities. Out-of-state incorporation does not eliminate qualification obligations in operating states. Separate internal governance choices from external regulatory duties. Identify which anticipated provisions the formation state permits, whether they must appear in the charter rather than bylaws, and whether the parties can administer them reliably.

sections.heading: Exam answer organization
sections.body: Compare at least two plausible forms using facts about control, liability, raising capital, transfers, tax, and compliance costs. Then give a reasoned recommendation with its disadvantages. A conclusion that simply names a form without connecting each important feature to a client objective omits the legal analysis. Do not reuse historical tax eligibility thresholds from the fifth edition as current numerical requirements.

examQuestions.question: A local business chooses an out-of-state corporate domicile solely because it is popular. What costs should the advice address?
examQuestions.answer: Compare governing law and desired flexibility with foreign qualification, duplicate fees or taxes, recurring administration, counsel familiarity, and the actual locations of operations. Popularity alone is insufficient.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Incorporation and Premature Commencement
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 3.3–3.11, 5.1–5.12, 6.1–6.7
guides.scope: The supplied fifth edition matches the outline. These notes cover the identified topics, not every proposition in every assigned section. Historical statutory and tax discussions are not a statement of current law.

sections.heading: Formation chronology
sections.body: Separate planning and promotion from filing and organizational action after filing. The book’s sequence includes financing arrangements, name reservation, selecting a registered office and agent, preparing and filing articles, paying fees, and conducting organizational meetings. Directors then organize governance through officers, bylaws, and authorized share issuances. Determine the point at which the governing statute recognizes corporate existence before analyzing who could act for it.

sections.heading: Promoter contracts
sections.body: A promoter’s agreement made before incorporation raises separate questions about the promoter’s liability and the later corporation’s liability. A nonexistent principal cannot itself have authorized a contract when it was signed. Review the contract’s language about the parties, intended obligor, and any condition that incorporation occur. The later corporation may adopt the arrangement, but adoption does not necessarily release the promoter. Identify an actual agreement substituting the corporation and discharging the prior obligor before concluding that a novation occurred.

sections.heading: Charter, bylaws, and statutory defaults
sections.body: Some provisions may be varied only in the articles; others may be placed in bylaws. Broad lawful-purpose clauses can allow operational flexibility, while an intentionally narrow purpose provision can constrain management. Determine whether a disputed term is permitted, properly located, and consistent with mandatory law. A charter is not merely a private deal among original founders because later investors also take interests under it.

sections.heading: Defects and equitable doctrines
sections.body: When filing or organization is defective, distinguish statutory liability provisions from de facto corporation and corporation-by-estoppel reasoning. De facto analysis concerns an attempted formation and operation under a valid authorizing law. Estoppel examines a party’s conduct in treating the enterprise as corporate and the context of the claim. Do not assume either doctrine survives unchanged under every modern statute. Build a timeline linking the defect, the contract or injury, the parties’ knowledge, and the later corrective act.

examQuestions.question: A promoter signs before incorporation. The later corporation adopts the contract. Has the promoter necessarily been released?
examQuestions.answer: No. Analyze promoter liability, corporate adoption, and a separate novation or agreement releasing the earlier obligor. Corporate adoption alone need not establish the required discharge.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Piercing the Corporate Veil
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. § 4.4, §§ 7.1–7.6; Macey, Moll & Hamilton, supplied 14th ed., ch. 6
guides.scope: The supplied fifth edition matches the outline. These notes cover the identified topics, not every proposition in every assigned section. Historical statutory and tax discussions are not a statement of current law. The casebook supplied is the fourteenth edition; the outline names the fifteenth.

sections.heading: Starting presumption
sections.body: Separate corporate existence is the starting point. A corporation’s debt is its own, and incorporation for limited liability is itself legitimate. A parent’s ownership of all shares or an individual’s complete control does not automatically make the controller liable. Identify the specific creditor, the unpaid obligation, the person or related entity sought to be charged, and the legal reason for crossing the entity boundary.

sections.heading: Operational separateness
sections.body: Relevant facts include separate accounts, accurate records, corporate decision-making, treatment of receipts, payment of personal expenses, and transfers among related companies. Explain how each fact shows genuine separateness or its misuse. The book treats intermingled affairs and disregard of formalities as important, but do not reduce a multi-factor inquiry to a single missed meeting. The governing jurisdiction and type of entity affect the weight of formalities.

sections.heading: Domination, capitalization, and injury
sections.body: Domination is commonly paired with an additional requirement involving fraud, illegality, or serious unfairness. Connect the alleged misuse to the creditor’s loss. Undercapitalization is a factor, especially where foreseeable tort risks arise, but insufficient assets after an ordinary business failure do not by themselves prove abuse at formation. Distinguish voluntary contract creditors’ knowledge of the entity from injured persons who had no opportunity to bargain for protection.

sections.heading: Case comparison and exam method
sections.body: Bartle refused to impose a subsidiary’s contract debts on its parent where separate indicia were maintained and the findings showed no fraud, deception, or injurious asset depletion. Use that result as a comparison, not a universal immunity for parent companies. Contrast facts showing deliberate diversion of assets or misleading treatment of the entities. Identify the governing test before applying ownership, control, records, capitalization, misuse, and the resulting inequity.

examQuestions.question: A subsidiary fails while its parent owns all shares. Is ownership alone enough to make the parent pay its contract debts?
examQuestions.answer: No. Start with separateness, identify the governing piercing test, and examine misuse, records, intermingling, capitalization, deception and the link to injury. Bartle illustrates the importance of additional facts.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Closely Held Corporations and Shares
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 16.1–16.12 and ch. 18
guides.scope: The supplied fifth edition matches the outline. These notes cover the identified topics, not every proposition in every assigned section. Historical statutory and tax discussions are not a statement of current law.

sections.heading: How investors obtain shares
sections.body: Distinguish an original subscription, a sale of treasury shares, and a transfer from an existing shareholder. An issuance brings newly created shares into investor ownership; a secondary transfer substitutes an owner of already outstanding shares. Authorized, issued, and outstanding describe different quantities. A share is the ownership interest, while a certificate is evidence of it. Do not infer that replacing or losing the certificate creates or extinguishes the underlying interest.

sections.heading: Price and consideration
sections.body: A subscription must establish an enforceable undertaking to take and pay for specified shares. Unpaid subscription liability ordinarily runs to the corporation, with creditor remedies depending on the applicable procedural and statutory framework. Par value is not market value. Where a statute retains par value, identify its particular legal consequences rather than assuming it measures economic worth. For no-par shares, directors may have pricing flexibility, but the form and valuation of consideration remain separate issues.

sections.heading: Payment and valuation
sections.body: The assigned discussion distinguishes statutes permitting traditional money, property, and completed services from provisions also accepting notes or future services. Identify the actual governing statute. The validity of the type of payment is distinct from whether the board valued it honestly. The book describes substantial deference to good-faith valuation and exceptions for fraud or deliberate overvaluation. Explain who challenges the issuance and what loss or statutory consequence is alleged.

sections.heading: Capital structure
sections.body: Debt creates repayment obligations and priority rights defined by the instrument and applicable law; equity allocates residual participation and governance rights. Preferred shares may divide dividend, liquidation, conversion, and voting rights from those of common shares. Read the charter and instrument rather than reasoning from the word preferred alone. Compare a bondholder’s contractual protections with a shareholder’s organizational rights, and evaluate leverage, payment obligations, priority, and dilution separately.

examQuestions.question: An investor buys shares from an existing holder. Is that necessarily an original issuance bringing new capital to the corporation?
examQuestions.answer: No. A secondary transfer changes ownership of outstanding shares. Distinguish it from an original subscription and a corporate disposition of treasury shares.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Preemptive Rights and Dilution
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. § 16.14
guides.scope: The supplied fifth edition matches the outline. These notes cover the identified topics, not every proposition in every assigned section. Historical statutory and tax discussions are not a statement of current law.

sections.heading: Purpose of preemptive rights
sections.body: Preemptive rights give qualifying existing owners an opportunity to subscribe proportionately to certain new issuances. Their purpose is to protect against dilution of economic participation and voting influence. Distinguish the existence of that opportunity from a guarantee that the corporation will never issue new shares. An investor who declines a valid proportional offer can still experience a reduced percentage holding.

sections.heading: Finding the source and scope
sections.body: The book describes different statutory and charter approaches, including denying a default right or recognizing a right only when affirmatively granted. Begin with the governing statute and charter. Identify the covered class, type of issuance, eligible holders, and any exception. Do not infer a universal preemptive right solely because the investor acquired shares first.

sections.heading: Proportionate analysis
sections.body: Calculate existing shares and voting power before the issuance, identify the total proposed new issue, and determine the eligible holder’s proportional allocation under the operative provision. Then test whether the offer honored notice, price, and timing requirements. Keep dilution of voting percentage distinct from whether an issuance transferred economic value by selling below an appropriate price.

sections.heading: Fiduciary issues remain
sections.body: Compliance with a preemptive-right clause does not necessarily resolve whether directors used issuance authority for an improper purpose or unfairly favored insiders. Conversely, the absence of a contractual preemptive right does not eliminate all fiduciary constraints. State the particular legal basis for the challenge rather than treating preemption as the only possible objection. Address the requested remedy and the effect on both the corporation and existing holders.

examQuestions.question: A minority investor claims a universal right to buy a proportional share of every new issue. What must be established first?
examQuestions.answer: Find the governing statutory and charter source, eligible class and covered issuance, including any exceptions. The assigned discussion describes different approaches; no universal entitlement should be assumed.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Shareholders, Directors and Voting
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 9.1, 9.3–9.8, 9.11–9.15, 11.5, 13.16, 13.20, 13.30

sections.heading: Who exercises management power
sections.body: The board has a collective governance role, while officers implement delegated operations. A majority shareholder is not automatically the corporation’s manager in a shareholder capacity. Distinguish selecting directors from controlling each board decision. A person who is simultaneously a shareholder, director, and officer must act through the powers and procedures associated with the relevant role.

sections.heading: Valid collective action
sections.body: Identify notice, quorum, voting requirements, and the governing documents for the particular meeting. The presence of enough directors does not necessarily cure defective notice. Traditional board action requires a duly convened deliberative body; statutes may authorize written action without a meeting. In the book’s discussed written-consent framework, unanimity protects a dissenting director’s ability to require collective discussion. Verify the operative statute before assuming electronic messages or separate informal approvals suffice.

sections.heading: Changing the board and voting arrangements
sections.body: For a vacancy, distinguish the authorized number of directors from the number actually in office and identify who may fill the particular seat. Cumulative voting can concentrate voting strength in support of a minority representative, but it is distinct from the ordinary rule for approving management action. Keep director elections, director removal, filling vacancies, and shareholder approvals in separate analytical boxes.

sections.heading: Exam checklist
sections.body: Identify the proposed action and institution with authority; find statutory and document requirements; count qualified participants; test notice, quorum, and votes; then consider a valid consent or later ratification if supported. Specify how an interested director affects the particular statutory calculation instead of silently counting or excluding that director. A substantively reasonable outcome does not itself cure a legally invalid procedure.

examQuestions.question: Directors separately send informal approvals. Does a majority of messages necessarily equal valid board action?
examQuestions.answer: No. Check the statute and governing documents, meeting rules, and any authorized written-consent procedure. The book’s discussed no-meeting route requires the relevant unanimity; separate messages are not automatically a lawful meeting.

sections.heading: Why close corporations create special risks
sections.body: In a closely held firm, ownership may be tied to employment, compensation, management participation, and an expected stream of distributions. Without a ready trading market, a minority owner cannot necessarily escape unfavorable treatment by selling. The same conduct that appears to be an ordinary management choice in a public company can therefore affect an owner’s entire investment arrangement.

sections.heading: Deadlock
sections.body: Identify whether the blockage concerns shareholder votes, board votes, or both, and what business action cannot occur. Equal ownership does not establish that every decision is deadlocked; examine actual voting rules and the disputed action. Determine what tie-breaking, buyout, voting, or succession arrangements the parties adopted. A dissolution request requires the applicable statutory ground, not merely interpersonal hostility.

sections.heading: Oppression and legitimate expectations
sections.body: A claim may concern termination of employment, denial of distributions, excessive compensation to controllers, exclusion from agreed management, or selective access to liquidity. State the jurisdiction’s theory rather than declaring that every disappointed expectation creates liability. Explain the investment-related expectation, the basis for treating it as legitimate, and any competing business justification. Separate harm to the corporation from an owner’s distinct individual injury.

sections.heading: Remedies and planning
sections.body: Compare dissolution, a buyout, enforcement of an agreement, and other relief available under the governing statute and case law. Valuation and who must buy can be as important as establishing wrongdoing. Donahue illustrates a particular jurisdiction’s concern with equal access to a corporate share purchase in a close corporation; it is not an all-jurisdiction rule governing every redemption. Planning provisions should specify valuation, triggering events, funding, and the mechanics of exit rather than relying on an informal promise to be fair.

examQuestions.question: Two equal owners disagree. What facts distinguish actual deadlock from ordinary disagreement?
examQuestions.answer: Identify the decision, voting body, applicable thresholds and actual inability to act, plus tie-breaking or exit arrangements. Equal ownership and hostility alone do not establish every statutory dissolution ground.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Duty of Care and Business Judgment Rule
references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 10.1–10.8; Macey, Moll & Hamilton, supplied 14th ed., ch. 10

sections.heading: Conduct standard versus judicial review
sections.body: The duty of care addresses what directors should do; the business judgment rule addresses when a court will defer to a decision. A bad result does not by itself establish a breach, and a favorable result does not prove an adequate process. Identify an actual decision, the information available, the time taken, and whether disinterested directors exercised judgment in good faith. Distinguish a decision from a failure to pay attention at all.

sections.heading: Information and attention
sections.body: The assigned discussion treats regular attendance and attention to corporate affairs as real responsibilities. Analyze how directors obtained information, questioned assumptions, used advisors, and responded to warning signs. Reliance is not a synonym for blind acceptance. Evaluate the reason for relying, the subject matter, and what directors knew or should have investigated under the applicable standard.

sections.heading: Comparing the case illustrations
sections.body: Shlensky involved objections to the Cubs’ refusal to install lights and play night baseball. The case illustrates why a court does not substitute business policy merely because an investor predicts a more profitable alternative. Smith v. Van Gorkom instead examined whether the merger decision was informed and concluded the process was deficient. Keep disagreement over business strategy separate from a claim that the board failed to inform itself before approving a major transaction.

sections.heading: Exam sequence
sections.body: Identify the alleged failure and responsible directors, state the governing care and review standards, assess process using concrete facts, and analyze causation and remedy separately. Check whether a charter provision or statute limits monetary liability and whether its exceptions apply; do not assume it extinguishes every duty or every type of relief. Explain why the facts support deference or rebut it rather than using the business judgment rule as a conclusion without analysis.

examQuestions.question: A board chooses an unpopular strategy after an informed, disinterested process, and the business loses money. Is loss alone a care breach?
examQuestions.answer: No. Separate the conduct standard from business judgment review and evaluate process, good faith and the applicable legal test. A disappointing outcome is not itself proof of deficient decision-making.

references: Cox & Hazen, Business Organizations Law, 5th ed. §§ 10.9–10.15, 11.8–11.10; Macey, Moll & Hamilton, supplied 14th ed., ch. 11A–E

sections.heading: Identify the conflict precisely
sections.body: A loyalty problem concerns the fiduciary’s personal interest or competing obligation, not simply an unsuccessful transaction. Identify the corporation, fiduciary, other party, financial interest, and decision influenced by that interest. Distinguish a transaction with the corporation, compensation, use of corporate property or information, and taking an opportunity that may belong to the corporation. Each category can involve different procedures and remedies.

sections.heading: Disclosure, approval, and fairness
sections.body: For an interested transaction, analyze what material facts were disclosed, who approved it, whether the decision-makers were disinterested, and which statutory route applies. Do not assume any shareholder vote automatically cures the transaction. Approval and substantive fairness are related but distinct issues, and the effect on validity, burden of proof, or review standard depends on the governing law. Marciano illustrates judicial examination of fairness despite an inability to obtain the usual disinterested approval in a deadlocked firm.

sections.heading: Corporate opportunities
sections.body: Ask how the fiduciary learned of the opportunity, the corporation’s activities and interest or expectancy, use of corporate resources, financial capacity as relevant under the governing test, disclosure, and the response of proper decision-makers. Taking an opportunity personally because management did not act immediately is not a complete defense. Equally, a business opportunity does not belong to the corporation merely because a director encountered it. Connect the facts to the jurisdiction’s actual test.

sections.heading: Who owns the claim and what follows
sections.body: A wrong to corporate assets normally creates a corporate claim; reduced share value alone does not automatically create a personal claim for each owner. Distinguish direct injury from a derivative claim and analyze the applicable procedural requirements before selecting a remedy. Fiduciary disclosure also requires separating the existence of a duty from the materiality of an omitted fact. A sound answer addresses conflict, process, substantive review, claimant, causation, and relief in that order.

examQuestions.question: A director benefits from a transaction approved by other directors. What facts must be examined before saying the conflict is cured?
examQuestions.answer: Identify material disclosure, disinterestedness and independence, voting requirements, the governing statutory route, substantive fairness and effects on review or burden. Approval alone is not a universal cure.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Overview of the Constitution
references: Supplied Constitutional Law detailed module notes, Module 1
guides.scope: Based on supplied study notes, not independently authenticated copies of the assigned judicial opinions. Case summaries remain review drafts. Historical cases are discussed for the assigned course, not as a complete statement of present law.

sections.heading: Constitutional structure
sections.body: Begin with the Constitution as a source of delegated powers, institutional design, and limits. Identify the government actor and the source of that actor’s authority before discussing whether its policy is desirable. Separate federalism, which distributes authority between national and state governments, from separation of powers, which distributes responsibilities among national branches. A dispute can implicate both dimensions.

sections.heading: Powers and rights are different questions
sections.body: Federal actors require a constitutional basis for action; state governments generally exercise a broader police power subject to constitutional limits. A claim that Congress lacks an enumerated power differs from a claim that an otherwise authorized measure violates a protected right. Work through both questions where the facts support them. Do not assume a legitimate governmental purpose alone supplies the missing constitutional authority.

sections.heading: Judicial role and analysis
sections.body: Judicial review operates through actual cases and controversies, so identify the court’s jurisdiction and the claimant’s ability to obtain the requested remedy. Constitutional supremacy does not eliminate procedural limits on adjudication. When reading an opinion, separate the governing text, the dispute’s procedural posture, the legal rule, its application, and the disposition. A judicial statement outside the ground necessary to resolve the case may have a different status from the holding.

sections.heading: Reading method
sections.body: For each assignment, make an actor–power–limitation–remedy map. Record which constitutional provision supports the power, which provision or structural principle limits it, and what a court could actually order. Use a case’s material facts to explain the boundary of the rule. The optional guide listed in the outline was not supplied, and a citation in the syllabus is not itself the underlying opinion.

examQuestions.question: Congress pursues a worthwhile policy. Does a desirable goal alone establish constitutional authority to act?
examQuestions.answer: No. Identify the government actor, the source and scope of delegated power, and any separate constitutional limitation. Policy desirability does not supply missing authority.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Federal Jurisdiction and Judicial Review
references: Supplied Constitutional Law detailed module notes, Module 2; assigned Marbury, McCardle, Martin and Cooper readings
guides.scope: Based on supplied study notes, not independently authenticated copies of the assigned judicial opinions. Case summaries remain review drafts. Historical cases are discussed for the assigned course, not as a complete statement of present law.

sections.heading: Two jurisdictional layers
sections.body: Federal judicial power must fit an Article III category and a statutory jurisdictional grant. A claim’s federal character does not answer every jurisdictional question. Distinguish the Supreme Court’s original jurisdiction from its appellate jurisdiction, and distinguish the constitutionally created Supreme Court from lower federal courts that Congress establishes. Identify the court and posture before discussing the merits.

sections.heading: Marbury and McCardle
sections.body: Marbury separates a legal right, the availability of a remedy in principle, and the jurisdiction of the court asked to supply it. The Court did not issue the requested writ because the claimed original jurisdiction exceeded Article III. McCardle concerns Congress’s withdrawal of the particular statutory appellate route used in a pending habeas appeal. It did not hold the detention constitutional or decide that Congress can eliminate every conceivable avenue of review.

sections.heading: Martin and Cooper
sections.body: Martin confirms that Supreme Court review can reach state-court judgments involving federal law; the source of the federal issue matters more than the tribunal in which litigation began. Uniform federal meaning and supremacy support that authority. Cooper addresses state officials’ obligation to comply with constitutional rulings rather than treating federal rights as optional when compliance provokes hostility. Keep state-court appellate review separate from the duty of state actors to obey controlling constitutional law.

sections.heading: Exam synthesis
sections.body: Ask which court is being asked to act, whether original or appellate authority is invoked, what Article III permits, what statute grants, and whether justiciability requirements are met. Then identify the legal issue and remedy. Explain why jurisdiction and merits are separate: establishing that government acted unlawfully does not automatically establish that this court can grant this form of relief. Use each assigned case for the specific institutional problem it resolved rather than citing all four as interchangeable statements of judicial power.

examQuestions.question: A plaintiff has a legal right and an appropriate remedy in principle. Must the Supreme Court grant that remedy in an original action?
examQuestions.answer: No. It still needs the constitutionally and statutorily required jurisdiction. Marbury separates entitlement, remedy and the power of this tribunal to supply it.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Justiciability: Standing
references: Supplied Constitutional Law detailed module notes, Module 3; assigned standing cases
guides.scope: Based on supplied study notes, not independently authenticated copies of the assigned judicial opinions. Case summaries remain review drafts. Historical cases are discussed for the assigned course, not as a complete statement of present law.

sections.heading: Constitutional minimum
sections.body: Analyze injury in fact, traceability, and redressability separately for each plaintiff, claim, and requested remedy. A concrete, personal injury must be actual or sufficiently imminent rather than an abstract desire for government compliance. Traceability asks whether the challenged conduct materially explains the injury; redressability asks whether the requested judicial relief would likely alleviate it. Uncontrolled third-party decisions can create problems for either inquiry.

sections.heading: Lujan and Lyons
sections.body: Lujan’s members had an interest in observing wildlife, but vague future plans did not establish imminent personal injury. The requested relief also raised redressability problems. Lyons shows why past injury may support a damages claim while failing to establish the future threat needed for an injunction. Do not convert evidence of a completed unlawful act into proof that the same plaintiff will personally experience it again.

sections.heading: Organizations, taxpayers, and third parties
sections.body: Organizational representation of members requires identifying an affected member and the relationship between the claim, the organization’s purpose, and individual participation. United Food allows statutory modification of the prudential participation restriction, not abolition of Article III injury. Flast recognizes a narrow taxpayer exception tied to taxing-and-spending action and a specific constitutional limitation. Eisenstadt illustrates third-party-rights reasoning in a prosecuted distributor’s challenge, not a general permission to litigate anyone’s rights.

sections.heading: Statutory labels and answer structure
sections.body: The course’s discussion of Air Courier uses zone-of-interests terminology. Keep that statutory cause-of-action inquiry distinct from the constitutional minimum, and flag the terminology rather than merging it into injury in fact. Structure an answer plaintiff by plaintiff and remedy by remedy. Identify the personal stake, causal chain, practical effect of relief, and any additional representational or statutory issue. A strong merits argument does not cure a standing defect.

examQuestions.question: A previously injured plaintiff seeks damages and an injunction based only on the past event. How should standing be analyzed?
examQuestions.answer: Separately for each remedy. A completed personal injury can support damages, while an injunction requires an adequate showing of a future personal threat, as Lyons illustrates.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Political Questions and Sovereign Immunity
references: Supplied Constitutional Law detailed module notes, Module 5; assigned political-question, state-ground and immunity cases

sections.heading: Political question
sections.body: Start with the particular issue and Baker’s factors rather than declaring every politically important lawsuit nonjusticiable. Textual commitment to another branch and the absence of judicially manageable standards require explanation from the constitutional provision and requested decision. Baker allowed the equal-protection claim to proceed. United States v. Nixon concerned a concrete evidentiary dispute; Nixon v. United States concerned Senate impeachment procedures. Reversing the case names reverses the lesson.

sections.heading: Adequate and independent state grounds
sections.body: Supreme Court review cannot change a judgment independently sustained by adequate state law. Identify every ground, remove the challenged federal ground, and ask whether the result would remain. Michigan v. Long addresses an ambiguous decision appearing primarily federal or interwoven with federal law and the effect of a plain statement of independent state-law control. Do not confuse this limit on review with a federal court’s discretionary abstention despite jurisdiction.

sections.heading: Defendant, forum, source of law, and remedy
sections.body: For sovereign immunity, identify each defendant and each requested form of relief. A damages award payable by the state treasury differs from prospective relief directed to an official to end an ongoing federal violation. Edelman bars retroactive monetary relief disguised as an injunction. Pennhurst prevents using the federal-law rationale of Ex parte Young to obtain a federal order compelling state officials to follow state law.

sections.heading: Waiver and abrogation
sections.body: Analyze clear state consent separately from congressional abrogation. Abrogation requires clear statutory intent and a constitutionally sufficient source of power. Fitzpatrick recognizes the significance of Fourteenth Amendment Section 5; Kimel requires examining whether the particular statute validly enforces the underlying constitutional right. Do not stop after finding that Congress mentioned states. Compare the right, the record of constitutional violations, and the remedy’s scope. Address each prospective, retrospective, official-capacity, and personal-capacity claim distinctly.

examQuestions.question: A state official is sued for future federal-law compliance and payment for past violations. Is a single immunity conclusion enough?
examQuestions.answer: No. Separate defendants, forum, legal source, capacity and remedy. Prospective federal-law relief and retrospective treasury payments raise different issues under the supplied immunity notes.

sections.heading: Constitutional source and procedural stage
sections.body: Identify the right, its source, the government action challenged, and the stage of the criminal process. Federal constitutional protections, state constitutions, statutes, procedural rules, and supervisory doctrines can supply different grounds. A rule applicable in a federal prosecution does not automatically have the same source or reach in a state prosecution. Keep incorporation through the Fourteenth Amendment separate from the historical meaning of a particular Bill of Rights guarantee.

sections.heading: Gideon and the scope of the decision
sections.body: Gideon involved a defendant unable to afford a lawyer who was denied appointed counsel for a state felony trial. The Court rejected the view that appointed counsel in that setting depended on exceptional circumstances and treated assistance of counsel as fundamental to a fair adversarial trial. The assignment should not be summarized as a right to a free attorney in every interaction with government. Ask which proceedings and consequences are involved before extending the rule.

sections.heading: Comparisons and exam method
sections.body: Separate the Sixth Amendment assistance-of-counsel problem from Fifth Amendment interrogation safeguards. A person can have Miranda protections before the prosecution stage at which a Sixth Amendment right attaches. Conversely, a trial-stage right can matter even when no interrogation occurs. Record the stage, custody status, interrogation, formal proceedings, asserted right, and requested remedy in separate columns. The assigned Hurtado opinion is not reproduced by merely listing its citation; use the missing-source indicator for that unbriefed assignment.

examQuestions.question: Police question a person before formal prosecution, and the person later faces a felony trial without funds. Are all counsel questions governed by the same rule?
examQuestions.answer: No. Distinguish custodial-interrogation safeguards from attachment and trial assistance-of-counsel questions. Gideon addresses appointed counsel in the state felony-trial setting; analyze the stage and source of each right.

sections.heading: Identification theories
sections.body: Separate a Sixth Amendment counsel challenge from a due-process reliability challenge. Ask when adversary judicial proceedings began and what type of identification procedure occurred. A physical lineup, a showup, and a photographic display do not necessarily have the same counsel analysis. Do not assume that any suggestive identification is governed only by one constitutional provision.

sections.heading: Due process and reliability
sections.body: The supplemental identification chapter discusses police-arranged suggestiveness and reliability. Examine the witness’s opportunity to observe, attention, prior description, certainty in the relevant framework, and time elapsed. Describe the procedure and governmental involvement before applying the test. A finding that a process is suggestive does not by itself answer whether the resulting identification must be excluded. Nor does the absence of a particular counsel right automatically resolve a separate due-process argument.

sections.heading: Bail and remedies
sections.body: Pretrial release raises an independent inquiry concerning appearance, conditions, the applicable statutory framework, and constitutional limits. Separate a claim that an amount is excessive from an assertion of an unconditional right to release. The outline assigns Kirby and Stack; the short supplied OCR pages concern identification discussion and do not establish that every assigned page or case has been fully supplied. Avoid treating a supplement chapter as proof of completion of the treatise reading.

sections.heading: Identify the protected interest
sections.body: Before asking whether police needed a warrant, determine whether governmental conduct was a search or seizure. Katz concerns interception of a private telephone conversation even without physical entry into the booth. Its rejection of a purely place-based or physical-entry approach does not convert every governmental observation into an invasion of a general constitutional right to privacy.

sections.heading: Keep privacy and property routes separate
sections.body: Jones identifies installation and use of a GPS device on a vehicle as an information-gathering physical intrusion on a protected effect. The property-based analysis remains available alongside the privacy approach associated with Katz. A conclusion that movements could be observed in public does not by itself dispose of an actual physical-intrusion theory. Identify precisely what was attached, entered, observed, or recorded.

sections.heading: From search to remedy
sections.body: A finding of a search begins rather than ends Fourth Amendment analysis. Identify the claimant’s own protected interest, the justification asserted, scope, and any warrant or exception. Then address exclusion separately. Do not say that Jones resolved every question about all location tracking or that Katz invalidates any recording. Mapp is assigned, but a general reference to exclusion does not substitute for a fully sourced brief of that opinion.

references: Modern Criminal Procedure: Cases, Comments, Questions, 15th ed., chapters 6 and 7

sections.heading: Define what requires justification
sections.body: Identify whether the state conduct is a search, a seizure of property, or a seizure of a person. A warrant application must connect the facts to the place, person, or evidence targeted. Probable cause evaluates the factual basis in context rather than requiring proof beyond a reasonable doubt. Keep an officer’s factual information separate from conclusions that simply repeat the statutory language.

sections.heading: Warrant validity and execution
sections.body: A warrant analysis should separate the issuing authority, factual basis, particularity, and how the warrant was executed. Even a valid authorization does not necessarily permit every later investigative act. Ask whether officers remained within the authorized location and scope and whether a new intrusion required an independent basis. A lawful initial presence is not a blanket license to manipulate or inspect everything encountered.

sections.heading: Assigned examples and limits
sections.body: Franks is identified in the supplied chapter’s discussion of challenges to an affidavit’s veracity; Hicks is assigned for a distinct additional-search problem. Do not collapse a challenge to the warrant’s factual foundation into a challenge to execution. For each issue, identify the alleged defect, its significance to the authorization, and the remedy. sections.heading: Encounter, stop, and arrest
sections.body: Identify the moment and method of restraint. A consensual conversation is not automatically a seizure, and a stop is not automatically an arrest. Explain the facts that change the category rather than attaching a label to the entire encounter. sections.heading: Terry requires two justifications
sections.body: The investigative stop must have a sufficient particularized basis, and the protective frisk requires a separate safety rationale involving a reasonable belief that the person is armed and dangerous. Suspicion of criminal activity alone is not an automatic authorization for a weapons search. In Terry, repeated observation of men apparently checking a store supplied context; the officer did more than act on an unexplained feeling.

sections.heading: Scope and escalation
sections.body: A protective frisk is directed at weapons rather than a general search for evidence. Explain why the chosen manner and duration fit the safety concern, and identify any later fact justifying escalation. A useful answer divides the encounter into initial approach, restraint, frisk, discovery, and any further search. If one stage is invalid, trace its consequences without assuming that every later item is automatically admissible or automatically excluded.

examQuestions.question: An officer has grounds for an investigative stop and automatically frisks the person for evidence. What separate inquiries are missing?

sections.heading: Chimel rationale
sections.body: A search incident to a lawful arrest is justified by officer safety and preservation of accessible evidence. Identify the arrestee’s person and the area within immediate control rather than treating arrest as authorization to search every nearby room or container. The scope must remain tied to the reasons for the exception.

sections.heading: Gant and the vehicle problem
sections.body: Gant rejects a reading of Belton that allows a vehicle search after every recent occupant’s arrest. One route concerns an unsecured arrestee within reaching distance at the time of the search. A separate vehicle-specific route asks whether it is reasonable to believe evidence of the offense of arrest might be found in the vehicle. Explain each route independently; a secured arrestee can defeat the first without logically deciding the second.

sections.heading: Independent exceptions
sections.body: Do not merge search incident to arrest, a vehicle evidence search supported by the applicable justification, consent, and an inventory rationale. Each has its own trigger and permitted scope. Gant involved a suspended-license arrest, a secured suspect, and cocaine in a jacket on the backseat; those facts explain why neither the accessibility rationale nor a search for evidence of that offense justified the search. The assigned Opperman reading requires separate inventory analysis rather than a label borrowed from Gant.

examQuestions.question: After a suspended-license arrest, a handcuffed occupant is locked in a patrol car. Does the arrest automatically authorize searching a jacket in the vehicle?

sections.heading: Consent as a distinct theory
sections.body: A consent argument requires examining whether consent was voluntary, whether the person had authority relevant to the search, and what scope was actually permitted. sections.heading: Undercover conduct and entrapment

sections.heading: Separate violation and exclusion
sections.body: Begin by identifying the specific constitutional violation and whose rights were affected. Then determine whether the challenged evidence was obtained through it. Exclusion is a remedy with its own scope and exceptions; neither the existence of a violation nor an officer’s assertion of good intentions alone resolves admissibility.

sections.heading: Trace the evidence
sections.body: Draw a timeline for statements, physical objects, witness information, and later police actions. For derivative evidence, explain the causal relationship to the initial illegality and test the actually applicable doctrine: an independent lawful source differs from attenuation of an existing causal link. Do not assume that any intervening event automatically cures the original violation. Identify the facts that matter under the assigned case rather than listing exception names.

sections.heading: Leon’s distinct inquiry
sections.body: Leon examines objectively reasonable reliance on a judicially issued warrant later found unsupported by probable cause. The analysis asks whether exclusion would serve the deterrence rationale in the circumstances and recognizes limits on reasonable reliance. It does not say that an officer’s subjective good intentions validate an unconstitutional search. Keep the warrant’s legal defect separate from the remedy and explain why reliance was or was not objectively reasonable. sections.heading: Three linked questions
sections.body: Identify evidence favorable to the defense, suppression or nondisclosure attributable to the prosecution, and materiality. Favorability can include impeachment as well as directly exculpatory information. The significance of an item depends on the charges, defense theory, witnesses, and record as a whole. sections.heading: Bagley and witness incentives
sections.body: The supplied chapter uses Bagley to develop the Brady obligation. Bagley involved undisclosed arrangements providing payment incentives to important government witnesses despite a defense request concerning inducements. That setting illustrates how information affecting credibility can matter even if it does not independently establish innocence. Ask what the undisclosed material could have done to the fact-finder’s assessment of the government’s case.

sections.heading: Materiality and separate preservation questions
sections.body: The reasonable-probability formulation concerns confidence in the outcome, not a requirement that the defendant prove with certainty that acquittal would have occurred. Evaluate the combined significance of the suppressed evidence rather than isolating each item artificially. Distinguish a failure to disclose existing evidence from loss or destruction of material, which the outline addresses through Trombetta. These are supplemental notes on the topic; the assigned treatise pages and all preservation decisions are not certified complete.

sections.heading: Identify the trigger
sections.body: The Miranda framework concerns custodial interrogation, not every conversation between a suspect and an officer. Analyze custody and interrogation separately and identify the time each condition began. Distinguish the underlying privilege against compelled self-incrimination from the procedural warnings used to protect it. A statement can raise a voluntariness question even where a particular warning issue is absent.

sections.heading: Warnings, waiver, and invocation
sections.body: Record which warnings were given, whether a legally sufficient waiver occurred, and whether the person later invoked silence or counsel. The fact that warnings were read does not automatically establish every element of waiver. Separate initial waiver from the rules governing renewed questioning after invocation. A later answer does not erase the need to analyze how police obtained permission to proceed.

sections.heading: Interrogation beyond direct questions
sections.body: Innis includes express questions and their functional equivalent: police words or actions, apart from those normally attendant to custody, that officers should know are reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response. The focus is not solely on an officer’s stated intention. Innis itself found the short conversation about a missing gun insufficient on the record to constitute interrogation. Apply the test to the known circumstances rather than declaring any overheard police conversation an interrogation.

examQuestions.question: Officers read warnings, obtain a signature and begin questioning. Does the signature conclusively prove an adequate waiver?
examQuestions.answer: No. Examine the required knowledge, understanding and voluntariness under the applicable rule, along with custody, interrogation and invocation. Miranda rejects replacing the safeguards with a boilerplate assertion.

sections.heading: Build a chronology

sections.heading: Fifth and Sixth Amendment separation
sections.body: The Miranda counsel safeguard addresses custodial interrogation; the Sixth Amendment assistance-of-counsel right concerns adversary criminal proceedings and its own framework. sections.heading: Speedy trial balancing
sections.body: Barker evaluates length of delay, reasons, assertion of the right, and prejudice together. Delay is not assessed by a single constitutional number applicable to all cases. Identify which periods count and why the prosecution or defense caused them. A defendant’s failure to demand trial is relevant but not an automatic waiver of the constitutional protection.

sections.heading: Pleas and informed choice
sections.body: A guilty plea changes the litigation posture and requires its own validity inquiry. Identify the defendant’s understanding of the charge and consequences relevant to the governing rule, voluntariness, counsel, and the record supporting acceptance. Do not treat an attractive bargain as conclusive proof that the plea was valid or that no earlier claim can matter. State which challenge survives the plea under the applicable assignment.

sections.heading: Jeopardy and the second proceeding
sections.body: Before asking whether a new prosecution is prohibited, identify when jeopardy attached, how the first proceeding ended, who requested termination, and whether the same offense or a distinct issue is involved. A mistrial, acquittal, dismissal, and conviction have different consequences. The outline’s Perez, Kennedy, Lee, and Johnson assignments require these distinctions. Avoid the shorthand that any second courtroom appearance is unconstitutional.

examQuestions.question: A defendant experiences lengthy delay but makes no early demand for trial. Is the constitutional claim automatically waived?

sections.heading: Jury entitlement and waiver
sections.body: The right to a jury depends on the nature of the offense and the governing seriousness threshold, not merely the label criminal. sections.heading: What facts change authorized punishment
sections.body: The supplemental sentencing chapter presents the distinction between facts used to select a sentence within an authorized range and facts that increase the legal maximum. Identify the maximum authorized by the verdict before evaluating the additional fact-finding; a legislature’s label alone does not answer the constitutional question.

sections.heading: Do not combine every sentencing issue
sections.body: Discretion over sentencing information, constitutional limits on capital punishment, and jury allocation of aggravating facts are different subjects. The outline assigns Williams, Furman, and Apprendi for those reasons. State the procedural rule and the particular restriction actually implicated. sections.heading: Identify the review vehicle
sections.body: Direct appeal, discretionary review, and collateral relief are not interchangeable. sections.heading: Self-representation
sections.body: Faretta concerns a defendant’s informed choice to conduct the defense personally at trial. A knowing choice can require awareness of the disadvantages of self-representation without requiring the defendant to demonstrate the expertise of counsel. sections.heading: Habeas and source quality
sections.body: The supplied scanned material includes discussion of procedural default, exhaustion, timeliness, and federal habeas review, but OCR quality and incomplete pagination prevent treating all assigned sections as complete. sections.heading: Three different threshold failures
sections.body: Newdow, Murthy and FDA v. Alliance concern access to adjudication, but their reasoning should not be collapsed into one slogan. Murthy concerns traceability and redressability through independently acting platforms. FDA v. sections.heading: From comparison to application
sections.body: For a new problem, ask whose injury is asserted, how the challenged defendant caused it, and how the proposed order would relieve it. A third-party representative must establish the legally relevant relationship; a causal chain must identify concrete links through intermediaries. An organization does not establish an injury merely by choosing to spend resources opposing a policy. Distinguish injury to operations from disagreement and voluntary advocacy spending. Do not infer a decision about a policy’s constitutionality or legality from dismissal on a threshold ground. sections.heading: Forum and source of law
sections.body: Alden and the 1984 Pennhurst decision identify different limits on ways around state immunity. Alden concerns a private federal damages claim in state court and the asserted use of ordinary Article I power. Changing the forum did not by itself defeat the nonconsenting state’s immunity. Pennhurst concerns a federal order directing state officials to obey state law. Labeling the requested relief prospective did not bring that claim within the federal-law rationale for Ex parte Young. Identify defendant, forum, source of the duty and remedy before selecting a supposed exception.

sections.heading: Compare rather than generalize
sections.body: Read these decisions beside Edelman’s distinction between prospective compliance and retrospective treasury payments and Fitzpatrick’s recognition of valid Section 5 enforcement authority. No one factual label resolves the entire inquiry: a suit against an official still needs the relevant federal-law basis, and a federal statute still needs a legally sufficient basis for abrogation. Distinguish the 1984 Pennhurst immunity decision from the 1981 Pennhurst decision separately listed in the spending-power assignments. Similar party names do not make the decisions interchangeable. These are review notes drawn from the supplied study material, not a substitute for absent primary opinions or later-law research.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Justiciability: Timing
references: Poe v. Ullman, 367 U.S. 497 (1961)
guides.scope: Original notes based on the identified historical judicial opinions retrieved from a documented CourtListener mirror. This is partial coverage of the assigned reading list, not a current-law certification or proof every assigned decision was supplied.

sections.heading: Timing is distinct from merits
sections.body: Justiciability asks whether this dispute is suitable for adjudication now. Ripeness concerns a controversy asserted too early; mootness concerns whether a previously live controversy has ceased. The doctrines must be analyzed using the requested remedy and actual facts. Poe is the supplied primary anchor for the pre-enforcement side of this module. Its refusal to adjudicate did not validate the challenged contraception restrictions on the merits. The newly retrieved source does not supply all other timing cases assigned in the outline.

sections.heading: Why Poe was dismissed
sections.body: Patients and a physician sought declarations concerning Connecticut restrictions before the prosecutions they feared had occurred. The opinion announcing the judgment emphasized a long enforcement history and the actual prospect of prosecution, not only the fact that legislation remained on the books. The Court’s members differed over the justiciability analysis. Distinguish the plurality’s reasoning, a concurrence in the judgment, and dissenting views rather than attributing every paragraph to a unanimous Court.

sections.heading: How to analyze a pre-enforcement problem
sections.body: Identify the exact conduct the plaintiff wishes to undertake, the prohibition alleged to cover it, actual enforcement actions or threats, and the practical harm of waiting. Compare those facts with the historical enforcement record discussed in Poe. A theoretical legal disagreement or the mere existence of a statute should not replace an explanation of the controversy. Equally, do not turn Poe into a universal requirement that a person first violate a law and accept punishment before any challenge is possible.

sections.heading: Connections and limits
sections.body: For an answer about timing, first separate standing, ripeness and mootness rather than using them as interchangeable labels. Explain what has happened and what still depends on contingencies. If the question raises later cessation, recurrence or duration of injury, identify the additional assigned doctrine needing a source. Roe and the remaining module opinions have not been treated as supplied merely because their names appear in the outline. This guide addresses Poe’s historical threshold issue, not current contraception or abortion rights.

examQuestions.question: Hypothetical: a plaintiff cites an old criminal statute but identifies no recent enforcement or concrete threat. What does Poe require the analysis to examine?
examQuestions.answer: Examine the actual controversy, intended conduct, enforcement history and realistic prospect of enforcement, and the reasons for deciding now. Distinguish the threshold question from whether the statute is constitutional; do not turn Poe into a universal rule requiring prosecution first.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Necessary and Proper Clause
references: McCulloch v. Maryland, 17 U.S. 316 (1819)
City of Boerne v. Flores, 521 U.S. 507 (1997)

sections.heading: Enumerated ends and implementing means
sections.body: McCulloch separates a legitimate constitutional end from the means Congress selects to accomplish it. The Constitution need not list every instrument Congress may use in executing an enumerated power. The opinion treats incorporation of a national bank as an implementing measure rather than requiring a freestanding express bank clause. Explain the relation between the asserted end and chosen means; the Necessary and Proper Clause is not a substitute for identifying a constitutional objective.

sections.heading: Appropriateness and constitutional limits
sections.body: The classic formulation permits appropriate means plainly adapted to a legitimate end when they are not prohibited and remain consistent with the Constitution’s letter and spirit. That is not an assertion that any useful policy is valid. Identify the power being implemented, how the measure advances it, and any independent prohibition. The case also concerns a state’s attempt to tax a federal instrument, which raises supremacy and the ability to frustrate federal operations rather than merely another question about Congress’s preferred policy.

sections.heading: Enforcement is not rewriting the right
sections.body: City of Boerne examined RFRA in a dispute over a church building permit. The Court distinguished enforcing Fourteenth Amendment protections from changing the underlying substantive constitutional standard. Its congruence-and-proportionality formulation asks about the injury to be prevented or remedied and the fit of the chosen legislation. Identify the constitutional right, relevant state conduct, evidentiary justification and reach of the remedy instead of assuming that Congress’s use of an enforcement label establishes authority.

sections.heading: Exam comparison and source caution
sections.body: Analyze the source of power before selecting a standard. A measure implementing an enumerated end and a statute asserted to enforce a constitutional right raise related but distinct questions. Do not apply a single unexplained reasonableness test to both. The McCulloch mirror’s reporter page is inconsistent with the assigned citation; its identifiable opinion text supports these doctrinal notes, but its apparent page markers should not be used as authenticated pinpoint citations. Other assigned cases remain separate readings.

examQuestions.question: Why must an answer distinguish a legitimate congressional end from its chosen means?
examQuestions.answer: The implementing-means analysis needs an identified constitutional objective and a sufficient relationship to it, with independent constitutional limits preserved. Merely describing a policy as useful or calling a measure necessary does not establish the whole inquiry.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Commerce Clause
references: United States v. Lopez, 514 U.S. 549 (1995)
United States v. Morrison, 529 U.S. 598 (2000)

sections.heading: Classify the asserted commerce power
sections.body: Lopez identifies channels of interstate commerce, instrumentalities and persons or things in commerce, and activities substantially affecting interstate commerce. Choose the relevant category before applying its test. The Gun-Free School Zones Act at issue addressed possession in a school zone without the interstate-commerce connection the government needed under the challenged theory. Do not assume that a local act is unreachable simply because it occurs within one state; explain why the asserted category does or does not cover it.

sections.heading: Nature of the activity and the causal chain
sections.body: The opinion distinguishes the regulated conduct from a lengthy series of effects on education, economic productivity and the national economy. If every link rests on a very broad generalization, explain why the proposed theory would lack a meaningful stopping point. Evaluate the activity, statutory elements, relation to a broader scheme and the particular constitutional theory rather than substituting the conclusion that the issue is important.

sections.heading: Morrison’s two sources of power
sections.body: Morrison rejected the federal civil remedy for gender-motivated violence under the theories before the Court. Its commerce discussion addressed noneconomic violent conduct and the claimed aggregate economic consequences. Its Fourteenth Amendment analysis separately addressed the state-action boundary and the remedy directed at private conduct. Congressional findings did not themselves decide the constitutional limit. Identify the claim against the actor and the source of authority separately.

sections.heading: Comparisons and unreviewed assignments
sections.body: When comparing Lopez and Morrison, focus on the regulated conduct, jurisdictional connection, inference chain and legal basis rather than equating all intrastate activity with invalidity. Distinguish state regulation from federal enumerated-power analysis. Raich is also assigned but was not located in this retrieval; these notes do not claim to resolve its broader-regulatory-scheme analysis from a missing primary text. Use a separate verified source before treating that part of the reading as complete.

examQuestions.question: Hypothetical: Congress supports a law regulating local noneconomic conduct with findings about its national economic effects. Does that alone answer the commerce issue?
examQuestions.answer: No. Classify the asserted category, examine the conduct, statutory connection and inference chain, and apply the relevant limits. Morrison shows that findings do not themselves establish constitutional authority; additional theories such as Section 5 need separate analysis.

guides.title: Detailed reading notes — Taxing and Spending Clause
references: South Dakota v. Dole, 483 U.S. 203 (1987)
National Federation of Independent Business v. Sebelius, 567 U.S. 519 (2012)
